turns.userMessage: I want a week of proper mountain hiking in the Alps in early July. Plan it for me.
turns.finalText: Early July is prime time in the Chamonix valley — snow-free trails up to about 2,500 m and long daylight. Here's a 7-day plan based from Chamonix: warm up on the Aiguillette des Houches, hike to Lac Blanc beneath the Aiguilles Rouges, traverse the Grand Balcon Nord to the Mer de Glace, and finish with the Albert 1er glacier viewpoint above Le Tour. I've based it on comfortable half-board mountain refuges and valley hotels, with the Flégère and Montenvers lifts to save your knees. Estimated cost: £1,650 including flights to Geneva, transfers, half-board refuge and hotel nights, and lift passes. Want me to book out the day-by-day details?

turns.userMessage: That's over budget for me — I can only spend £1,200 all-in. Make it cheaper.
turns.finalText:
Done — same valley, same summits, £1,080 all-in. The mountains are free; it was the refuges and lifts costing you, so the revised plan cuts those.

Here's what changed to make it cheaper: you'll camp at a riverside campsite in Chamonix (£13/night, hot showers, Mont Blanc from your tent door) instead of half-board refuges; every route now starts on foot from the valley floor rather than a lift, which turns each day into a proper mountain day; and breakfasts and picnics come from the supermarket, with one celebratory fondue at the end. Budget airline seats to Geneva run about £120 return in early July if you book about six weeks out, and the shared shuttle to Chamonix is £25 each way.

The week itself keeps its shape: Aiguillette des Houches to warm up, Lac Blanc climbed the honest way from Les Praz, the Grand Balcon Nord to the Mer de Glace, and the Albert 1er glacier snout above Le Tour to finish. Full breakdown: £240 travel, £91 campsite, £140 food, £560 left as buffer for kit, one bad-weather lift ride and that fondue — £1,080 against your £1,200 ceiling.

If a storm rolls in, the £560 buffer also covers a night in the Chamonix youth hostel dorm to dry out. Want the day-by-day details locked in?

days.title: Lac Blanc the honest way
days.description: The valley's classic viewpoint, climbed on foot

activities.notes: 1,400 m up without the lift — start early; the lake mirrors the Drus by mid-morning

activities.activity: Descend to Les Praz and recover with a river dip
Roll along the Petit Balcon Sud path above the valley
activities.notes: Gentle recovery day to keep legs fresh for the balcony traverse

activities.activity: Supermarket resupply and route check for tomorrow

days.title: Grand Balcon Nord to the Mer de Glace

activities.notes: Steady height gain on foot instead of the cable car — glaciers across the valley all day

activities.activity: Look over the Mer de Glace from Montenvers then walk back down
activities.notes: Skipping the rack railway saves £36 and the descent path is lovely

activities.activity: Hike from Le Tour village up the moraine path towards the Albert 1er refuge

activities.activity: Descend for the one splurge: fondue night in Chamonix
Saturday market wander and pack down the tent
Bus back to Geneva airport for the flight home
